themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK, a 338% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 5.2 per week (z-score: 5.31), suggesting rapid deterioration of road surfaces, potholes, or street infrastructure across Morrisania/Crotona.
evidence: 23 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (338% spike)
Z-score of 5.31 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Correlates with traffic signal complaints (62 last week, 386% above baseline), suggesting broader street infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: On-the-ground inspection of which streets are most damaged and what caused the rapid deterioration
Interview residents about how potholes, cracked pavement, or sidewalk conditions are affecting mobility and vehicle damage claims

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints jumped to 62 LAST WEEK, a 386% spike above the 8-week baseline of 12.8 per week (z-score: 4.6), indicating widespread malfunctioning signals that could pose safety and congestion risks.
evidence: 62 traffic signal complaints last week vs. 12.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (386% increase)
Z-score of 4.6 indicates high statistical significance
Overlaps temporally with street condition spike, suggesting coordinated infrastructure degradation
reporting_angles: Identify specific intersections with broken signals and document traffic/safety impact with video or resident testimony
Query DOT on response time and backlog for signal repairs in this district

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about illegal animals kept as pets jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike over the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69), marking an abrupt emergence of animal welfare or public health concerns.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical significance
Represents emergence of a pattern that was essentially non-existent in prior 8 weeks
reporting_angles: Interview residents and animal control officers about what species are involved and what prompted the sudden spike
Investigate whether this reflects a single building/landlord issue or broader community trend

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints reached 5 LAST WEEK, a 3900% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 14.74), indicating a sudden collapse in sanitation services or accumulation of debris across the district.
evidence: 5 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 is exceptionally high, indicating unprecedented spike
Correlates with residential disposal complaints (5 last week, 264% above baseline), suggesting broader sanitation service failure
reporting_angles: Document which neighborhoods have visibly dirty streets and ask Sanitation Department why service has deteriorated
Canvass residents about accumulation of litter and impact on neighborhood quality of life

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints increased to 16 LAST WEEK, a 94% spike over the 8-week baseline of 8.2 per week (z-score: 3.91), contributing to an ongoing pattern of residential disturbances in the district.
evidence: 16 noise complaints last week vs. 8.2 weekly baseline (94% increase)
Z-score of 3.91 indicates statistical significance but more moderate than concurrent spikes
Part of broader pattern: noise complaints rank #2 overall in district (3836 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Categorize noise sources (construction, music, traffic) and identify hot spots driving the recent increase
Interview residents about sleep disruption and quality-of-life impact
